To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of antibodies against the pneumococcus in children with primary immunodeficiencies are low and can be improved by the use of immunoglobulin replacement.

in immunodeficient children receiving immunoglobulin, antibody concentrations against most pathogenic serogroups reached levels that are considered to be protective against invasive pneumoccocal infection.

in IVIG-treated PID children, trough levels of specific antibodies against most pneumococcal pathogenic serotypes are ≥ 0.2 µ g/ml (a protective level), and trough PnPsAbs correlate with PnPsAb in IVIG product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the prevention of pneumococcal disease in patients with PID.
the development of a new generation of IVIG products, which will be adapted to the specific needs of patients.
the development of a new method of treating patients with PID, which will improve the prevention of infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrates that IVIG replacement therapy in children with PID is able to maintain protective levels of antibodies against most pathogenic pneumococcal strains.

the study shows that the IVIG product used in the study provides a good protection against the pneumococcal infections in the patients studied, and that this can also be extrapolated to the other patients with PID.
IVIG treatment of children with PID provides a good protection against pneumococcal infections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the levels of antibodies in the IVIG products are not always sufficient to protect the patient from infection, so it is important that the levels of these antibodies be measured to make sure that the IVIG product is working as intended.

the levels of pneumococcal antibody in patients receiving IVIG were similar to those in healthy adults and in the IVG product, which suggests that IVIG replacement therapy provides sufficient protection against invasive pneumococcus.
we have demonstrated that the levels of antibodies in the blood of children with PID who receive IVIG are protective against invasive pneumonococcal disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

trough levels of PnAbs in children with PID treated with IVIG are in the range of those found in healthy individuals and that trough levels of the PnAbs in the IVIG products correlate with trough levels in children with PID.
the IVIG product should contain a high content of the most common serotypes, and the dose should be adjusted to the patient’s body weight.
the levels of antibodies against the most prevalent pneumococcus serotypes in patients treated with IVIG are similar to the levels of these antibodies in healthy adults.
